Markdown and MDX - Frontmatter
text_content:
Frontmatter is a YAML like key/value pairing that can be used to store data about a page. `` does not support frontmatter by default, though there are many solutions for adding frontmatter to your MDX content, such as:
[https://github.com/remarkjs/remark-frontmatter](https://github.com/remarkjs/remark-frontmatter)
[https://github.com/remcohaszing/remark-mdx-frontmatter](https://github.com/remcohaszing/remark-mdx-frontmatter)
[https://github.com/jonschlinkert/gray-matter](https://github.com/jonschlinkert/gray-matter)
`` does allow you to use exports like any other JavaScript component:
Metadata can now be referenced outside of the MDX file:




A common use case for this is when you want to iterate over a collection of MDX and extract data. For example, creating a blog index page from all blog posts. You can use packages like [https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html](https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html) or [https://www.npmjs.com/package/globby](https://www.npmjs.com/package/globby) to read a directory of posts and extract the metadata.

text_content:
React does not natively understand markdown. The markdown plaintext needs to first be transformed into HTML. This can be accomplished with `` and ``.
`` is an ecosystem of tools around markdown. `` is the same, but for HTML. For example, the following code snippet transforms markdown into HTML:
The `` and `` ecosystem contains plugins for [https://github.com/atomiks/rehype-pretty-code](https://github.com/atomiks/rehype-pretty-code), [https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype-autolink-headings](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype-autolink-headings), [https://github.com/remarkjs/remark-toc](https://github.com/remarkjs/remark-toc), and more.
When using `` as shown above, you do not need to use `` or `` directly, as it is handled for you. We're describing it here for a deeper understanding of what the `` package is doing underneath.

title: Deep Dive: How do you transform markdown into HTML? - code_1
code_content:
import { unified } from 'unified' import remarkParse from 'remark-parse' import remarkRehype from 'remark-rehype' import rehypeSanitize from 'rehype-sanitize' import rehypeStringify from 'rehype-stringify' main() async function main() { const file = await unified() .use(remarkParse) // Convert into markdown AST .use(remarkRehype) // Transform to HTML AST .use(rehypeSanitize) // Sanitize HTML input .use(rehypeStringify) // Convert AST into serialized HTML .process('Hello, Next.js!') console.log(String(file)) //

Hello, Next.js!

}
